items.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023
items.q: I took a couple lessons with Armando Ghitalla and the first thing he asked me, I played something and he liked it

ctx.x: They have one of those bands here in nearby Utica, it’s called the Red Band. And I find them a fascinating social thing with the men and women marching around and the stamina it must have taken for some of those events.

Yeah. We would start the feast on the day before and we would start at 8 in the morning. Italian bands, however, don’t march in step, they just walk. They don’t march in step, they just walk and play. Because all the marches, the old Italian marches, they’re like little overtures, They’re not like “Stars and Stripes Forever” all the way through it. They’re very musical and everybody doesn’t play at once and it’s like a little mini- overture. So we used to do that 8 to 12 noon, and take a break and then go across…

numbers while they shot the fireworks. And we did the same thing the next day. And four trumpets. We all did all of it. And I guess nobody ever told us we were supposed to get tired. But we just played. It took a lot of endurance.
